transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-24
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Recording: Auto
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Rafael (Redwood SE), Priya (Orchid Head of Security), Tom (Platform Eng), Lina (IT Ops), Evan (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial):
Redwood walked through SSO/SAML metadata exchange, SCIM provisioning flow, and proposed RBAC least-privilege mapping. Customer asked about audit logs, KMS/HSM integration, data residency, and private deployment trade-offs. Agreed next steps: share SAML metadata, SCIM test token, SOC2/ISO docs, and map RBAC roles.

Topics:
- SAML SP/IdP handshake and metadata exchange
- SCIM provisioning and user lifecycle events
- RBAC model: roles -> permissions -> joiners/leavers process
- Audit logs: retention, export, SIEM integration
- Encryption: KMS/HSM support and key rotation
- Data residency / VPC and private deployment considerations

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — im Maya, AE on this account, and Rafa — Rafael is our security-focused SE. we'll run through SSO, SCIM, and RBAC patterns and then talk about compliance stuff. sound good?
[00:12] Priya (Orchid): yes thanks. main goals for us: we need least-privilege by default, full auditability for user provisioning, and proof of controls for SOC2 and ISO. we're also evaluating hosted vs private because of investor PII.
[00:28] Rafael (Redwood SE): great. high level we'll show the SAML flow, the SCIM provisioning lifecycle, and a recommended RBAC matrix. i'll flag places where hosted requires additional controls or where a private deployment simplifies things.
[00:40] Tom (Orchid): quick question before we start — do you support single-attribute mapping for group claims? we currently rely on an attribute called orchid:team in our IdP.
[00:54] Rafael: yes, we support custom attribute mappings, and you can send group claims or roles. small caveat: if you want per-token claim validation for downstream apps we have a mapping layer in the console. sometimes the transcriptor calls it, um, the mapping table, but it's essentially a claims transform.
[01:10] Lina (Orchid): and provisioning — we have automated onboarding via SCIM today with Okta, we want to know how Redwood will reconcile duplicates and handle email changes.
[01:22] Rafael: good one. by default SCIM runs as upsert. we do an email-based match, but we can configure alternate matching keys (e.g., employee id). dedupe is best-effort during the sync and we surface a reconciliation report. note: if you need guaranteed no-merge semantics we can set a stricter matching rule, but that affects how invites are handled.
[01:45] Priya: about audit logs — we need immutable audit trails, show who did what and when. retention policy is 7 years for some regs. can we export to our SIEM and sign logs with KMS?
[01:57] Maya: yes, logs include actor, IP, operation, object id, and delta. we can stream to your syslog/Splunk/Datadog via secure forwarders and also export cyclic snapshots. Rafael, correct me if i'm wrong on signing?
[02:10] Rafael: we support envelope signing of audit bundles using customer-managed keys through KMS. for private deployments we can integrate HSM-backed keys. for hosted we support bringing your own key in supported clouds, but we usually rotate keys on a set schedule unless you opt for BYOK.
[02:29] Evan (Orchid): so hosted BYOK is available? our legal prefers customer-managed keys.
[02:36] Maya: yes, BYOK supported for enterprise plans — you'll have to go through KMS setup and we provide a runbook. for full HSM-backed signing we recommend private deployment.
[02:48] Tom: about data residency — we need data to remain in eu-west-1. does Redwood allow region pinning for logs and model caches?
[02:58] Rafael: region pinning is available. for hosted we can restrict storage and log exports to eu-west-1, but some ephemeral caches may live in nearby regions for performance. if absolute residency needed, private deployment with regional-only compute nodes is the safe path.
[03:15] Priya: ok that explains trade-offs. can you outline what the SAML setup looks like practically? metadata exchange, cert rotations, assertion attributes.
[03:26] Maya: sure. step 1: Redwood provides SP metadata (ACS URL, Entity ID, certificate). step 2: your IdP ingest the SP metadata and maps attributes. step 3: we test a login and inspect assertions. cert rotation is either automatic on our side with notification or you can manage the certificate in your IdP. we also support signed assertions and encrypted assertions if you need attribute encryption.
[03:50] [Timestamps in meeting, mild crosstalk] Speaker 1: so do we need SAML2.0 only or OIDC?
[03:58] Rafael: we support both SAML 2.0 and OIDC. many enterprise customers use SAML for SSO and OIDC for token-based service-to-service auth.
[04:10] Priya: encryption at rest — are models or tokens stored in plaintext anywhere?
[04:17] Rafael: tokens and secrets are always encrypted at rest. model weights are not considered customer data in the typical workflow but any cached KV or prefixes derived from requests are encrypted at rest and you can enable additional envelope encryption. note: the transcript may show "K V cash" sometimes but it's KV cache in runtime.
[04:35] Lina: about RBAC specifics — we need a role for auditors with read-only access to audit logs and a separate role for ops to manage provisioning but not data exports. how granular can you get?
[04:47] Maya: RBAC is resource-scoped. you can create roles at org, team, or project levels, and tie permissions to API routes, console actions, and log access. we also have attribute-based controls for time-limited elevation.
[05:02] Tom: can we integrate with our existing SSO groups so that group membership maps to roles automatically?
[05:08] Rafael: yes, through SCIM and group-to-role mappings. we have three mapping strategies: claim-to-role, group-sync, and AD/LDAP bridge. claim-to-role is the least invasive.
[05:25] Priya: I want to be explicit: do you store PII fields from users in your DB? we need to know retention and deletion flow for GDPR.
[05:34] Rafael: we store minimal identity fields required for provisioning (email, name, employee id if provided). PII retention is configurable and you can request data deletion; we have retention windows and a purge run. for GDPR we provide an export and deletion job and can include proof-of-deletion logs.
[05:53] Evan: legal also asked about subprocessor list and SOC2 scope.
[05:57] Maya: we'll send the current subprocessor list and SOC2 Type II report. we also publish our ISO27001 statement of applicability.
[06:05] [pause]
[06:15] Tom: slightly worried about provisioning loops — if SCIM sync and a downstream identity orchestration system both try to update attributes, do you provide conflict resolution rules?
[06:27] Rafael: yes, we have a configurable precedence policy: IdP-first, Redwood-first, or last-writer-wins, and we surface a conflict audit so you can triage.
[06:39] Priya: for auditability — will the logs show SCIM delta payloads and the raw SAML assertions, or are those redacted?
[06:48] Rafael: we log metadata of assertions (issuer, subject, attributes) and can capture raw assertions on demand for troubleshooting, but storage of raw assertions is opt-in due to sensitivity. we also have redaction rules for sensitive attributes.
[07:05] Maya: note on retention and export formats: logs can be exported as JSONL bundles, compressed and signed. we can push those to your S3 bucket with server-side encryption using your KMS key.
[07:19] Lina: about key rotation — if we rotate keys in KMS every 90 days, will it break SAML cert validation?
[07:28] Rafael: we support key rollover patterns. for SAML signing certs you can publish both old and new certs in metadata during a rollover window. for KMS envelope keys, we handle decryption of older keys as long as the CMK's key policy allows it.
[07:44] Priya: one of our compliance controls requires separation of duties — the person who can run exports cannot change RBAC rules. is that achievable?
[07:54] Maya: yes, you can create a role that has export rights but explicitly lacks RBAC management. we also integrate with SSO to allow just-in-time elevation that is logged and requires approval if you want that.
[08:07] Tom: network-wise — if we go private, what's the typical on-prem footprint?
[08:13] Rafael: private can be VPC-deployed with dedicated GPU nodes, the control plane runs in your VPC or in our managed control plane with a private connectivity tunnel. we provide deployment manifests and an ops runbook. typical footprint depends on throughput but the minimum includes a control plane node, worker nodes, and storage endpoints.
[08:33] [Interruption] Speaker 2: sorry, did you say dedicated GPU nodes for private?
[08:37] Rafael: yes dedicated nodes, which gives you deterministic throughput and isolation.
[08:42] Priya: for the pilot we prefer a scoped private deployment just to validate SSO, SCIM, and logs. what's the timeline?
[08:49] Maya: if legal signs the MSA and we get PO, we can spin a scoped private pilot in 2-3 weeks; hosted pilot faster. Rafael will provide the kickoff checklist.
[09:00] Priya: can you talk about least-privilege onboarding flows for contractors and seasonal staff — we need temporary access that auto-expires.
[09:09] Rafael: we have time-bound role assignments integrated with SCIM and can support ephemeral access tokens tied to a request/approval workflow. you can set max TTLs and require re-approval.
[09:22] Tom: integration with our IAM — we use Azure AD and also have an identity broker. any known issues?
[09:29] Rafael: Azure AD + SCIM is a common pattern. the only gotcha is group paging in large tenants — you may need incremental group sync. we can supply a connector that handles paging and rate limits.
[09:45] [15 minutes pass in meeting — summarized]
[24:50] Rafael: demoing a short SCIM provisioning trace now — creating a user, mapping to role 'platform-admin-lite', and showing the audit record. see the right-hand panel for actor, request id, and delta.
[25:10] Tom: i see the delta; is that captured in the log stream we can pull to SIEM?
[25:15] Rafael: yes, the same payload can be forwarded in near-real time to your SIEM or to S3 for batch ingest.
[25:28] Lina: when you forward near-realtime, what's the SLA on delivery and is the stream encrypted in transit?
[25:36] Maya: encrypted over TLS, and delivery SLA depends on the forwarder; we guarantee at-least-once delivery but we surface delivery status and retries.
[25:48] Priya: any demo notes about false positives in role mapping?
[25:52] Rafael: we expose a dry-run mode for SCIM where you can preview mappings and see what role assignments would happen without committing. helps catch false positives.
[26:10] Evan: cost question quickly — does private deployment increase our license and infra costs?
[26:16] Maya: yes private includes a platform fee and infra costs, but it gets you BYOK, HSM, and stronger residency guarantees. we can model numbers once we know throughput.
[26:27] Tom: procurement would like a checklist of security controls for internal review.
[26:32] Maya: we'll attach a security checklist and a short runbook with the metadata and command examples.
[26:40] [Short pause while Rafael pulls a doc link in chat]
[26:55] Rafael: pasting the SCIM sample payload in chat — sample attributes, group mapping, and conflict rules. also added a link to our RBAC pattern doc.
[27:10] Priya: for SOC2 audit the auditor wants access to historical user provisioning logs and evidence of least-privilege enforcement. do you provide auditor access or do we export bundles?
[27:22] Rafael: best practice is to export signed bundles to your S3 and share that with auditors. for live access we can create a read-only auditor role with MFA and IP restrictions that only exposes logs and not configuration.
[27:38] Priya: if we give an auditor read-only access, can we limit their view to a specific time window?
[27:45] Rafael: yes, time-scoped access tokens and temporary views are supported. we log the auditor's actions as well.
[27:55] Tom: about change management — how do RBAC changes get propagated? is there an approval workflow?
[28:02] Maya: we integrate with ticketing systems (Jira/Ticketing) for approvals; changes can be gated by an approval workflow and recorded in the audit.
[28:12] Priya: ok this is good. let's talk about a slightly exotic case — machine accounts that need access for model scoring but should never be able to export trained outputs. how do you prevent that?
[28:24] Rafael: create a machine role with specific API route permissions that allow scoring endpoints but forbid export and data dump routes. we also support network egress controls to block exfil.
[28:37] Priya: egress controls — can you restrict outbound to only our approved endpoints?
[28:43] Rafael: in private yes; in hosted we provide egress allowlists and per-tenant firewall rules.
[28:50] Tom: small note — we have compliance that requires immutable WORM storage for certain logs for 7 years. do you support WORM buckets?
[28:59] Rafael: we can stream to S3 with WORM (S3 Object Lock) enabled on your side; Redwood can sign and push bundles but the retention enforcement happens in your bucket.
[29:12] [Noise on line, minor crosstalk]
[29:25] Priya: anything we should be cautious of during testing?
[29:28] Rafael: watch for group membership limits, rate-limits on SCIM calls and the matching key policy. we'll give you a test harness to simulate 10k users to validate performance.
[29:40] Maya: wrapping up next-step recap in a sec.
[29:45] Priya: one last question — we use a third-party secrets manager, HashiCorp Vault. can Redwood fetch secrets from Vault or do we need AWS KMS?
[29:55] Rafael: we integrate with Vault via a connector; we can retrieve secrets or use Vault as the primary KMS; integration requires additional config and the runbook covers it.
[30:08] [Demo ends — final Q&A]
[40:12] Maya: recap: we'll send SP metadata, SCIM token, SOC2/ISO docs, RBAC mapping template. customer will return a prioritized list of roles and the compliance controls they must see in the pilot.
[40:25] Priya: agreed. also will share list of attributes we consider sensitive for redaction.
[40:31] Tom: i'll confirm KMS choice and VPC peering windows, and Evan will handle procurement timelines.
[40:42] Evan: procurement aiming to review terms this week, target PO by end of next week if legal ok.
[40:50] Maya: excellent. Rafael, anything else to call out?
[40:54] Rafael: just that we'll provide a dry-run script for SCIM, and a small Dockerized test harness for private pilot to validate network and KMS integration.
[41:05] Priya: do you have a recommended baseline RBAC matrix we can start from?
[41:09] Rafael: yes — we'll attach a starter RBAC matrix with typical roles: admin, ops, platform-lite, auditor, readonly, contractor-temp.
[41:20] Maya: thanks all. we'll follow up with docs and the pilot kickoff scheduling.
[41:27] [closing chatter, confirm next steps]
[51:55] Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache). Links referenced in chat: SCIM-sample-payload.csv, RBAC-patterns.pdf, SAML-metadata.xml (will be included in follow-up email).

End of transcript.
